sections.h2: Where Montcalm County keeps its land records
sections.html:
Every Montcalm County deed lands in one place, the register of deeds in Stanton at 211 W. Main St. (box 368, Stanton, MI 48888). Call 989-831-7337 or email regofdeeds@co.montcalm.mi.us. Phone ahead for counter hours and for the electronic filing rules, since staff set both.

Stanton became the county seat in 1860, replacing Greenville. A parcel in any township of the county, from Carson City to Vestaburg, is recorded here.

Greenville is the largest city, with 8,816 residents in 2020. It lies 16 road miles southwest of Stanton and about 33 miles northeast of Grand Rapids, which explains why Montcalm is counted in the Grand Rapids metropolitan area. Lakes and the Flat River sit inside the city limits, and the Fred Meijer Heartland Trail ends in Greenville. A house near a lake or trail often draws a buyer who wants the recreation, so mention those features in your listing.

Carson City, in the southeast, lies along M-57, 20 miles by road from Stanton. Stanton itself is a government town of 1,348 residents in 2020. Farms around both cities mean many listings come with acreage, outbuildings or wells, so gather those records before you list.

The county counted 66,614 residents in 2020 and an estimated 69,406 by July 2025. Owners live in 83.1% of occupied housing. Half of owner-occupied homes were worth under $185,500 in 2020 to 2024 figures, and rent at the median ran $869.

The Revised Judicature Act prices recording at a flat $30.00 a document. Money is due with the paper, and an electronic filing gets one extra business day. Call Stanton to confirm the amount before you mail a check, and ask whether the office has a preferred way to receive electronic filings.

Montcalm County recording charges
ServiceCharge
Record a deed or other document$30.00
Each added instrument assigned or discharged in one paper$3.00
Copy, per page$1
Certificate on a recorded paper$5.00

The grantor owes both taxes. Michigan charges $3.75 and the county $0.55 on each $500 block of value, a partial block counting as a whole one, and the money must reach the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is handed over.

Family handovers get special treatment. The state act excludes a deed from a parent to a child or grandchild, and it excludes foreclosure deeds and deeds in lieu. The county act has no family exclusion, so the county share can still apply. Whichever exemption fits, write it on the deed itself.

MCL 565.201 gives the register grounds to refuse a paper, and a refusal costs a trip across the county. Hand your closing agent this short list before anyone signs.

  • Dark ink signatures, with every signer's name printed beneath and spelled as the notary spelled it.
  • Each grantee's mailing address, plus the preparer's name and address.
  • Roomy margins: 2.5 inches at the top of page one, half an inch around the rest.
  • One recordable event named on the opening line.
  • Letter or legal size sheets in 10-point type or larger.

Anything in a foreign language travels with an English translation, and a Social Security number has to be masked down to four digits.

sections.h2: How a sale changes taxes for the next owner
sections.html:
Between sales, In Michigan a house's taxable value can climb only 5% or the rate of inflation per year, whichever is lower. A transfer ends that protection, and the next owner's value jumps to state equalized value. A close relative who keeps a residence non-commercial can inherit without the jump.

Assessing is a city and township job in Michigan, not a county one, so your local assessor handles the paperwork even though the deed goes to Stanton. The new owner reports the transfer within 45 days.

Sellers who claimed the homestead exemption rescind it on Form 2602 within 90 days of moving out. Late filing runs $5 per day to a $200 limit, and the exemption ends December 31. New occupants file Form 2368 by June 1 or November 1.

sections.h2: Selling an inherited or run-down house
sections.html:
It can still sell. An heir signs through the personal representative, and a certified death certificate gets recorded when the deed names a survivor. A buyer who pays cash and takes the house as it stands skips lender appraisals and repair demands.

Before choosing a closing date, ask the county treasurer where the parcel stands on taxes, because any delinquent balance is cleaned up first. If you cannot reach the person named on the deed, a title company can tell you what paper the register will need.

Start with a finished deed from an attorney or title company, since register staff check that a paper meets recording standards but do not draft it. Sign in front of a notary, then walk through the checklist above with your agent. Send the original with the $30.00 fee, plus the transfer tax payable to the county treasurer, to the Stanton office or file it electronically. After recording, the buyer has 45 days to tell the local assessor.

If you live far from Stanton, an electronic filing through your title company saves the trip, though the office allows one extra business day for it. Ask for a copy of the recorded deed for your closing file. Keep it with your tax records, since you may need the date later.

Timing matters when you set a closing date. The recorded date is what fixes your buyer's place ahead of any later claimant, so closing agents usually send the deed the same day funds are released. If something is wrong with the paper, the register returns it, and the fix has to be made before the deed can be recorded.

Bring photo identification for the notary and the names of every owner exactly as they appear on the earlier deed. Know where the buyer's mailing address will be printed, because the register will not accept a deed without each grantee's address. Have the closing agent confirm the legal description, the preparer's information and the notary block before you sign anything.

If your house is part of an estate, collect the personal representative's papers and a certified death certificate for the record. If you moved out, remember the homestead exemption deadline on Form 2602. A cash buyer who takes the house as it stands can often close sooner, but the deed, the transfer tax and the recording steps are the same as in any other sale.

faqs.q: Where is a Greenville-area deed recorded?
faqs.a: Stanton's register of deeds, even for a Greenville address, because Montcalm County has a single recording office at 211 W. Main St. The phone is 989-831-7337.

faqs.q: How is the transfer tax calculated?
faqs.a: The state charges $3.75 and the county $0.55 for every $500 block of value, rounded up, and the seller pays within 15 days of delivering the deed. Some family transfers are exempt if the deed says so.

faqs.q: Will the register check my deed form?
faqs.a: Staff check that a paper meets recording standards and then record it. Drafting is outside their role, so bring a finished deed prepared by an attorney or title company.

faqs.q: How far is Stanton from Greenville?
faqs.a: About 16 miles by road. Carson City is roughly 20 miles from Stanton, so sellers in the south and west should allow time for an in-person filing.

faqs.q: What do I do about my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It has to be rescinded on Form 2602 with the local assessor within 90 days of moving out. A late filing is charged $5 per day up to $200.
